subject: Deployment packaging addendum & SLA credit request
messages:
From: Ryan O'Neill <ryan.oneill@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment packaging questions

Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete packaging and support options list for our VPC/on-prem rollout. High level asks:
- Clear breakdown of platform fee vs support seats (annual vs metered).
- Example SOW for a phased rollout (pilot -> prod).
- Any migration or go-live credits you can offer if performance falls short of our SLO during ramp.

Can you send the pricing matrix and a sample SOW we can circulate with procurement? Leah (cc'd on later replies) will lead contract redlines.

Cheers,
Ryan
Ryan O'Neill
Director, Infrastructure & AI
Acme Health

Attachment: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ryan O'Neill <ryan.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging questions

Ryan —

Appreciate the list. I attached a concise packaging grid and our canonical SOW template to make procurement's life easier: packaging-grid.xlsx, SOW-template.docx.

Quick summary:
- Platform fee: annual subscription for control plane + ops; SKU options for small/medium/large node counts.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours), Premium (24/7 with named SE), Enterprise (dedicated oncall + SLA credits).
- Migration credits: we typically offer migration engineering hours as a one-time credit on larger commitments; platform-fee credits are possible but evaluated case-by-case.

Given you mentioned SLO-linked credits, I'll loop in Karthik (sales engineering) and Hannah (CS lead for private deploys) to define an objective metric (e.g., P95 latency, tail tokens/sec for peak windows) and a measurable credit mechanism.

Next steps: 
1) Karthik to propose an objective performance metric and measurement window.
2) Draft addendum to SOW capturing ramp acceptance criteria and any fee credit.
3) Leah to provide procurement playbook / preferred contract language for redlines.

Files attached: packaging-grid.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), SOW-template.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ryan O'Neill <ryan.oneill@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging questions

Ryan / Marissa —

Quick technical proposal for a measurable SLA credit tied to go-live ramp:

Proposal summary:
- Metric: P95 inference latency for customer production queries over a rolling 24-hour window during the first 90 days post-go-live, measured at the token output boundary (end-to-end).
- Target: <= 450ms P95 for the agreed workload profile (we'll capture a sample 72-hour trace during pilot).
- Credit: If we miss target for more than 3 non-consecutive daily windows within the first 90 days, Redwood will apply a platform fee credit equal to 15% of monthly platform fee for the following month for each exceeding window, capped at 45% for the quarter.
- Conditions: Credits apply only if customer provides request traces and we can rule out customer-side network/configuration causes; load testing prior to go-live must match agreed profile.

Rationale: ties financial concessions to a clear, measurable customer experience while limiting downside for Redwood. We can codify in an addendum to the SOW; legal typically prefers a capped credit vs. service termination language.

Marissa — if you want, I can draft the addendum language and a sample measurement appendix.

-Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none
From: Ryan O'Neill <ryan.oneill@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Park <leah.park@acme.com>
Date: 2027-05-07T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging questions

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A few asks from our side before we circulate to legal: 
- Procurement prefers amortized platform fee treatment for the first 12 months; would Redwood consider a structured amortization (monthly credits) if we commit to a 24-month reserved capacity?
- On the credit metric: we'd like the credit to apply automatically (we'll share traces to validate, but credits should be applied unless Redwood demonstrates a force majeure / customer misconfig). The 15%/window approach is fine; could we tighten the cap to 60% for the first quarter?
- Please include the addendum as a separate DocuSign envelope and mark out the acceptance criteria in the SOW appendix so legal can sign off quickly.

Leah (procurement) — looped here to coordinate redlines.

Can you send a redlined addendum and a DocuSign link?

Best,
Ryan

Attachment: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ryan O'Neill <ryan.oneill@acme.com>, Leah Park <leah.park@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment packaging questions / Addendum v2

Ryan / Leah —

Appreciate the feedback. Attached: SOW-addendum-v2.docx with two changes per your asks:
1) Amortization language: optional 12-month amortization schedule included if customer signs a 24-month reserved capacity commitment (see Section 2.3).
2) Credit cap adjustment: increased first-quarter cap to 60% (from 45%) for larger reserved commitments as a one-time commercial concession.

Notes on automatic crediting: we can implement an "auto-apply" clause when traces are delivered within 10 business days of an exception; clause also includes a short dispute window (10 business days) where Redwood can demonstrate external causes. This keeps the process operationally tractable for both sides.

I've created a DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/ACME/SOW-addendum-v2 and uploaded the redline version to our deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-1572.

If Leah or legal want different language, we can iterate quickly. Proposed next step: Leah shares baseline redlines by EOD Wed and we'll produce the final DocuSign-ready file.

Files attached: SOW-addendum-v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
